I will keep my farm mainly in the wheat-maize system, because that is the most familiar and stable way for me to use my land, water, and labor. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I will not spread myself too thin with too much cotton, because cotton needs more field watching and more spraying. I will put 10.1 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and keep 3.0 mu in cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen for a strong stand, and irrigate three times because I have well water and I do not want to risk a dry spell reducing tillers and grain filling. After wheat harvest, I will put that same 10.1 mu straight into hybrid maize, keep fertilizer at a medium-high level, and use no-tillage to save labor and catch the season on time. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area, use hybrid seed, give more potassium than wheat and maize, and plan for more pesticide sprays because insects are usually a bigger risk there. I am choosing steady yields and manageable labor over pushing for the highest possible output.
